title: Binance Works to Recover Billions After Major Hack
summary:
On October 30, 2026, Binance said hackers had stolen digital assets worth more than $6.3 billion. Binance is a large exchange where people trade digital money, with more than 300 million registered users worldwide.

Binance said about $3 billion had been secured, but many assets were still in the hands of hackers no one has yet named. At first, it thought the break-in may have started with one engineer's laptop, but later it found more break-in points.

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the attack was not done by one person. He said the hackers used a tool that erased traces, making the investigation harder.

In the United States, the Secret Service said it was working to find, freeze, trace, and recover the stolen funds, and Binance said it was also working with the FBI.

Binance said its US-facing exchange was not affected. It told users their money was safe and that it was covering losses, setting aside more than $6.34 billion. Some experts warned customers to check their contracts, because a promise may not always be legally binding.
why_it_matters: It matters because it shows why keeping online accounts safe is important when you use the internet.

keywords.explanation: An exchange is a place where people buy and sell digital money.

Legally binding means a promise must be kept because the law says so.
